step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram represents SceneSoftware's 3D interactive application backend platform (Show in 3D). Web and Mobile clients submit resource processing requests through API Gateway. Depending on the asset type (images vs 3D models), API Gateway routes requests to dedicated Lambda functions: a group of Lambda functions processes and optimizes image resources through multiple steps, while a separate Lambda function processes 3D model optimization algorithms. Both sets of Lambda functions persist metadata into an RDS database and store optimized media assets in S3 buckets.

graph.name: SceneSoftware Show in 3D Interactive Platform Architecture
graph.notes: SceneSoftware platform enables users to create complex interactive 3D applications code-free, optimized for web, mobile, and desktop.

nodes.name: Web Client
nodes.notes: Web interface where users upload resources and access 3D applications.

nodes.name: Mobile Client
nodes.notes: Mobile device interface for accessing applications and uploading resources.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Entry point for APIs that routes incoming resource requests to appropriate Lambda functions.

nodes.name: Image Processing Lambdas
nodes.notes: A set of Lambda functions executing multi-step image optimization pipelines using Node.js, Python, or PHP.

nodes.name: 3D Model Processing Lambda
nodes.notes: Lambda function applying specific algorithms to optimize 3D models for interactive rendering.

nodes.name: RDS Database
nodes.notes: Relational database used to store resource metadata. Migration to Aurora is planned for cloud-native scaling.

nodes.name: S3 Buckets
nodes.notes: Object storage where processed image resources and 3D models are stored.
